name: ui-morphism
description: Named UI style languages as executable skills — each with measured token values, a performance budget and an explicit when-not-to-use. Descriptive and plural, not a design-quality tool: every skill fires on a named style or a concretely described one, never on "make it look good". Four plugins today — ui-morphism-core plus brutalism-ui, glassmorphism-ui and bento-grid-ui; seven further styles are researched in docs/ and not yet built.

plugins.name: ui-morphism-core
plugins.description: Shared foundation for the ui-morphism style skills: host-framework detection, the --um-<style>-<group>-<variant> token grammar and its emitters, the WCAG 2.2 contrast and CSS accessibility validator, the intensity 0-100 contract with its clamp and context-cap mechanisms, and the common audit-report format. Installed automatically as a dependency of any style plugin. Not a design skill: it decides nothing about how a UI should look.

plugins.name: brutalism-ui
plugins.description: One named visual language, applied on request: neubrutalism. Hard 2-5px ink borders, zero-blur offset shadows, flat saturated fills, chunky display type, and the hover-into-its-own-shadow interaction, with measured token values and an explicit when-not-to-use. Fires on the named style, not on general design-quality requests.

plugins.name: glassmorphism-ui
plugins.description: One named visual language, applied on request: glassmorphism. Backdrop-blur navbars, cards, modals and command palettes, with the @supports opaque fallback, the -webkit- twin, the four accessibility escape hatches and worst-case composited contrast measured at both extremes of the ground. Fires on the named style, not on general design-quality requests.

plugins.name: bento-grid-ui
plugins.description: One named layout pattern, applied on request: the bento grid. Asymmetric modular tiles where size encodes importance on a locked gutter — feature sections, dashboards, portfolio indexes — with spans assigned by content weight, DOM order held equal to reading order, and a per-tile audit. Fires on the named pattern, not on general layout or design-quality requests.
